title: 键盘管理器的新版编辑器开关会错乱

status.label: Consolidate with active toggle-state report #47962
status.detail: The reported new-editor toggle changes and unexpected remap output directly match the open #47962 report; no fix or upstream ownership is claimed.

judgment.rationale: The reporter describes editing switches in the new Keyboard Manager editor, closing it, then seeing unexpected key output and changed switch states on reopening. Open issue #47962 directly reports the same new-editor discrepancy between enabled/disabled toggles and actual remapping behavior, including remaps that remain active after a toggle is changed. #47962 remains open and has no assignee, so this is consolidation to an active covering report, not a claim that the underlying defect is fixed. The automatic duplicate label and bot suggestion are supporting hints only; the matching observable behavior is the basis for this judgment.
evidence: The issue reports PowerToys v0.99.1 and says new-editor switches change unpredictably after closing the editor, with unexpected key output and different switch states on reopening.
Open issue #47962 reports the same new-editor toggle/remapping-state mismatch and describes active mappings that do not match the displayed switch state.
#47962 remains open with no assignee and includes a PowerToys report ZIP; no linked fix or matching PR was found.
#46426 describes a visual toggle mismatch when switching between classic and new editor, while #47941 focuses on Allow Chords and random shortcut disabling; neither is as direct a match as #47962.
judgment.recommended_action: Keep #47962 as the active report for the shared new-editor toggle/remapping-state mismatch and avoid a competing fix proposal for #47965.

fix_assessment.rationale: This report is consolidated with the active same-symptom issue #47962 rather than receiving a competing fix proposal; this does not assert that a code fix has shipped.

issue_context.summary: The new Keyboard Manager editor reportedly changes toggle state unexpectedly after closing, and the resulting remappings do not match what the switches show.
known_information: The report lists PowerToys v0.99.1 and Windows 11.
The report says editing switches in the new editor, closing it, and typing in a text editor produces unexpected output; reopening shows changed switches.
The report has no uploaded PowerToys report and one automated duplicate-suggestion comment.
Open issue #47962 reports a direct mismatch between new-editor toggle state and actual remapping behavior.
inferences: The symptoms may be another manifestation of the toggle/profile synchronization problem described in #47962, but no code-level root cause or fix is established.
issue_context.analysis: A direct active report already captures the same observable behavior: new-editor toggles and actual remapping activation become inconsistent. The duplicate label and automated suggestion are not sufficient alone, but comparison with #47962's steps supports consolidation. #46426 is primarily a classic/new editor toggle display mismatch, and #47941 concerns Allow Chords and random disabling; keep those as related context rather than treating them as the closest tracker. No fix or owner is claimed.
initial_investigation: Read the Chinese issue body and translated its expected/actual behavior, then checked version, labels, comments, assignees, and report attachment state.
Compared the complete live report for #47962; its toggle-versus-remap mismatch is a direct match and the issue remains open without an assignee.
Compared #46426 and #47941 to distinguish a visual editor toggle issue and an Allow Chords-specific report from the closest covering behavior.
Searched for PRs referencing #47965; none were returned.

next_action.label: Consolidate with #47962
